Subject: Post-call: data handling & subprocessors (summary + next steps)

Hi Sara / Jacob - thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: real-time customer support assistant for payments (sanitized transaction context + user-entered text).
- Data concerns: PII handling, log retention, trace logging, and potential cross-border residency.
- 3rd-party telemetry / monitoring vendors you use: Sentry and Datadog (high level).
- Procurement ask: SOC 2 Type II and subprocessor list for review.

Questions / clarifications we promised to follow up on:
1) PII scope: what specific fields you consider PII in request payloads (names, emails, last4, full PAN, tokenized IDs) - will you confirm sample schema?
2) Retention: desired retention windows for raw request logs vs aggregated telemetry.
3) Logging controls: access controls for debug logs, redaction needs, and whether persistent KV caches are acceptable.
4) Subprocessors: list of telemetry, analytics, marketplace flows (e.g., if you plan to use Redwood via cloud marketplace).

Next steps we propose:
- Can you share your data-schema and current PII classification (attachment okay).
- We will share our most recent SOC 2 Type II summary, subprocessor roster, and a short security FAQ doc.
- Schedule a security deep-dive with our security lead (michael.grant@redwoodinference.com) - 45 minutes to go over retention, redaction, and residency options.

I attached a short subprocessor template you can fill (subprocessor_list.csv) - if easier, reply with an existing vendor list.

Thanks - I'll loop in our security lead and SE to prepare options for the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole

PII scope (high level): first_name, last_name, email, phone, last4 (PAN), token_id (we keep full PAN in vault, never send). We can provide a sample request payload (sanitized).
Retention: Our compliance target is 90 days for raw request payloads, 3 years for aggregated telemetry. Will need options for shorter windows (30/7 days) for higher-risk flows.
Logging controls: We need redaction at the SDK / client level for any fields marked PII and strict RBAC for access to raw logs.
Subprocessors: see attached vendor list (we include Sentry, Datadog, AWS, Google Cloud Marketplace flows).

Subject: Re: Post-call: data handling & subprocessors (summary + next steps)

Quick technical notes from my side after a first pass on their vendor list:
- SDK-level redaction: we support client-side redaction hooks and field-level tokenization. Recommend shipping a sanitize-before-send pattern for PII fields (we can provide an example middleware).
- Retention: runtime request logs are configurable; default hosted retention is 30 days but can be shortened to 7 days or extended on Dedicated/Private. For aggregated telemetry we can export to a customer-owned sink (S3/GCS) for 3+ year retention.
- KV cache persistence: we can keep per-request caches ephemeral; if they want long-lived caches we recommend encrypted, customer-key-managed storage (KMS).
- Marketplace flows: if using a cloud marketplace listing, there are additional subprocessors (marketplace billing and entitlement providers). We'll document those specific subprocessors per marketplace (AWS/GCP).

I'll draft a short tech appendix (redwood-security-sheet.pdf) showing config toggles and sample middleware. Michael - any compliance notes you want to add before I send?

- Dev
